scenes.title: The hospital contract
scenes.viewerPurpose: Picture a hospital keeping rights but losing practical control Notice a change of power without a visible coup
scenes.composition: A hospital’s ordinary work depends on an outside service operator
addOrChange: Add a rights document and recognizable supply connection, not a coup.

cues.narration: The hospital still has legal rights, but another organization controls the systems keeping it open.
cues.visualAction: The rights sheet remains intact while the service cable reaches outside control.

cues.narration: The Seventh Signature imagines power changing hands while everyday life appears to carry on.
cues.visualAction: Hospital staff continue working as the dependence becomes visible.

scenes.title: Power without a coup
scenes.viewerPurpose: Meet six fictional defenders of technological rule Hear promises whose consequences others would bear
scenes.composition: Six fictional thinkers sit at a discussion table
addOrChange: Add six ordinary figures and notes, avoiding villain lighting.

cues.narration: Six fictional thinkers argue for a world run by powerful technology organizations.
cues.visualAction: Reveal the six participants comparing their proposals.

cues.narration: They promise steady services and better decisions, but other people would live with those decisions.
cues.visualAction: Put service plans on the table with affected people visible beyond it.

scenes.title: Six persuasive voices
scenes.viewerPurpose: Feel the difficulty of arguing with sincere protectors See everyday digital systems as tools of power
scenes.composition: A continuity contract controls identity and service access
addOrChange: Add one login and one hospital service request as concrete dependencies.

cues.narration: Their argument is disturbing because they believe they are being responsible.
cues.visualAction: A participant checks the plan carefully, without malicious gestures.

cues.narration: Contracts, online identities, and cloud services become ways to decide who is really in charge.
cues.visualAction: Follow the contract to the access it can grant or withhold.

scenes.title: Hear the strongest case
scenes.viewerPurpose: Want to understand the appeal before judging it Ask how much freedom reliable services might cost
scenes.composition: A reader considers the strongest argument beside an appeal route
addOrChange: Keep the book and disputed service question without the final critique.

cues.narration: This political fiction asks you to hear the appeal before judging it.
cues.visualAction: The reader considers the proposal before responding.

cues.narration: How much freedom could disappear inside an arrangement that promises to keep everything working?
cues.visualAction: End where the appeal reaches the operator’s authority.
